title: credential-stager-and-async-stream-helpers-python-sdk
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: Added CredentialStager helper and new async_stream utilities; minor public API additions for session lifecycle. Backwards compatible by default; opt-in via new kwargs. Bump python SDK to v0.24.0.
description: Context: Several teams reported friction when integrating token rotation and bursty streaming workloads. This PR introduces a CredentialStager utility (lightweight prefetch + lease queue) and an async_stream helpers module to make backpressure-friendly async iterables easier to compose across long-lived streaming sessions. Motivation: reduce auth-related failed requests during token handoff and improve ergonomic composition for consumer code (less boilerplate around cancellations, reconnection hints, and graceful drains). Design goals: (1) keep public surface minimal and opt-in, (2) reuse existing credential interfaces so cross-SDK parity is achievable, (3) add telemetry hooks for future rollout. What this PR does: - Add redwood_sdk/credentials/stager.py (CredentialStager): prefetches refresh tokens, exposes acquire/lease/release semantics, supports pluggable backoff policies. - Add redwood_sdk/streams/async_helpers.py: provides async_partitioned_iter, drain_with_timeout, and a small stream combinator (zip_async) that preserves cancellation semantics. - Wire CredentialStager into streaming client internals as an optional parameter (client ctor kwarg: credential_stager). - Add docstrings, examples, and migration notes in docs/streaming.md and examples/streaming/credential-stager-example.py. - Tests: unit tests for stager lease behavior, integration test that simulates token expiry during an ongoing stream, and a small e2e that exercises reconnection with pre-warmed credentials. Related: coordinated with TS/Go SDK maintainers to align API shapes (see ENG-1292). Rollout: default behavior unchanged; customers must opt-in to enable stager via new kwarg. Migration: guide included to show how to pass existing credential providers into the stager. Checklist: - [x] Implementation - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Docs and example - [x] CI green - [x] Cross-SDK API proposal posted
commits: feat(cred): add CredentialStager with lease/prefetch semantics
test: add unit/integration tests for stager and stream helpers
small_snippets:
# usage example
from redwood_sdk.credentials import CredentialStager
from redwood_sdk import StreamingClient

stager = CredentialStager(provider=my_provider, prefetch=2, lease_ttl_seconds=30)
client = StreamingClient(api_key=None, credential_stager=stager)
async for chunk in client.stream(...):
    process(chunk)

# partitioned_iter example
async for batch in async_partitioned_iter(source_iter, max_batch=32):
    await handle_batch(batch)
review_comments: Ethan Park: A couple of nits on naming (lease -> hold?) and a question about fairness when multiple streams compete for staged tokens. Please add docstring examples for the fairness behavior.
Marisol Vega: Addressed naming nit; added fairness notes and an optional fifo argument to CredentialStager. Also added an integration test that opens 3 concurrent streams and asserts no starvation.
Sofia Chen: Tests look solid. Can we add a lightweight benchmark to show latency impact when stager is enabled vs disabled?
Marisol Vega: Added scripts/benchmarks/stream-prefetch-small.py and included results in the PR description. Observed median tail-token-latency reduction of ~18% under synthetic load.
Liam O'Connor: One security review item: ensure we never log raw tokens. Audit confirmed no token prints; added a guard in stager to redact potential token reprs.
Security Bot (automated): SAST scan flagged no secrets in code. Note: test fixtures contain mock tokens only.
ci_summary: CI: 24 jobs (unit tests, linters, type checks, integration). First run: 2 flaky integration failures (timeouts) on matrix linux-python3.11; retried and green. Coverage: +0.6% on streams package. Lint: one minor typing import issue fixed in follow-up commit.
notes_for_release: v0.24.0: Add CredentialStager and async_stream helpers. Opt-in feature to improve token handoff for long-lived streams. See docs/streaming.md for migration and examples.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-1299: propagate CredentialStager shape to TS/Go SDKs and add cross-SDK examples
ENG-1301: add telemetry metrics for stager hits/misses and lease durations
ENG-1302: evaluate queuing strategies under high-concurrency workloads
backcompat_rationale: Default behavior unchanged; credential_stager is optional and accepts existing provider objects. Public client surface expanded but existing callsites remain valid.
changelog_entry: Added CredentialStager (opt-in) and helper utilities for async streaming; bump to v0.24.0.
acknowledgements: Co-authored with Priya Nair (TS SDK) and Jonas Müller (Go SDK) for cross-SDK parity discussions.
